1) the diffusion coefficient of water in multicomponent particles can be extracted using Fickian diffusion models; 2) the diffusion coefficient is found to be a strong function of particle composition, with an increase in water diffusion constant observed for increasing organic fraction in the particle; 3) the diffusion coefficient in multicomponent systems is found to be in excellent agreement with the diffusion constant in a binary system, suggesting that the diffusion of water is largely independent of the identity of the co-s

1) the diffusivity of water in organic particles can be extracted from measurements of particle size change during dehydration, and 2) the vapour pressure of an SVOC can be determined from measurements of particle growth during exposure to a gas phase containing the SVOC.
we have developed a method to simultaneously investigate diffusion and evaporation of both water and a semi-volatile organic compound from a ternary organic aerosol particle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a comprehensive understanding of the physicochemical changes that occur during the drying of organic particles.
the development of experimental techniques and modelling approaches that can characterise the evaporation kinetics and diffusional mixing in multicomponent organic particle systems.

the development of a general methodology to investigate diffusion of water and SVOCs in multicomponent organic particles, which may be applied to studies of the physicochemical changes that occur during the dehydration of organic aerosol particles in the atmosphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diffusion and volatilisaton in multicomponent particles are both important, but that their relative contributions to observed size evolution can be decouped, allowing for their separate treatment.
the evaporation of water from a multicomponent aerosol particle is governed by diffusion in the particle phase.

the diffusional mixing and evaporation of SVOCs is an additional factor to consider in the interpretation of size evolution of ternary organic aerosols, and that the diffusion constant of a component in multicomponent particles can be extracted from the particle size evolution, even when it is a minor component.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the diffusivity of water in multicomponent organic particles can be treated as an ideal solution, while that of a SVOC is best treated as a non-ideal solution.
the evaporation of water from viscous ternary aerosol particles is dominated by diffusion of water in the particle, while that of a SVOC is controlled by the vapour pressure of the SVOC.
we have shown that diffusion and volatility of water and SVOCs can be treated separately, even in multicomponent systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple, yet rigorous approach can be used to extract the diffusion and volatility parameters of water and semivolatile organic components from a single particle experiment.
the evaporation of water from multicomponent particles is not a simple process.
the evaporation of a SVOC can significantly affect the observed size evolution of a multicomponent organic particle.
